name: Struct Packing Visualizer
blurb: alignment of struct members and the padding bytes wasted
intro: Paste C struct definitions and see each member's offset, size and alignment, the padding the compiler adds, and a byte map. Layout follows the chosen ABI (ARM Cortex-M with short enums, ESP32/RISC-V 32, x86-64 SysV, Windows x64, i386, AVR), honours __attribute__((packed)), #pragma pack and #defines for array sizes, and suggests a smaller member order.

inputs.label: C code
inputs.help: Structs, unions, typedefs and #define sizes. Types defined earlier in the paste can be used by later ones.

inputs.label: Packing
inputs.help: Applies to every struct; #pragma pack and packed attributes in the code apply too.

examples.title: A sensor frame with 12 bytes of padding on Cortex-M
A packed message header with bit-fields and a nested struct

usage: Give code as C source with one or more struct/union definitions (typedefs, nested structs, arrays with #define sizes, bit-fields, __attribute__((packed)), #pragma pack are understood), abi = armeabi | mcu32 | lp64 | win64 | i386 | avr, pack = natural | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8, and optionally which struct to show. Returns sizeof, alignment, total padding, a table of offset/size/alignment/padding per member, the size after reordering by alignment, static asserts to pin the layout, and a layout object with the byte map (cells with start, len, label, kind). Use it before putting a struct on the wire, in flash or in shared memory.
sources: ARM Procedure Call Standard for the Arm Architecture (AAPCS, IHI 0042), sections 5.1 and 7.1
System V Application Binary Interface, AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement, section 3.1.2
System V ABI Intel386 Architecture Processor Supplement, table 2.1
Microsoft Learn, x64 ABI conventions: types and storage, bit-field layout
avr-gcc ABI (GCC wiki): type sizes, byte alignment
